entertainment.title: Live Nation Adds Venue on Australia’s Gold Coast
entertainment.summary: Surfers Music Hall will be a 2,500-capacity live music space in Surfers Paradise, with a target to open its doors in mid-2028.
entertainment.body:
GOLD COAST, Australia — Live Nation continues to expand its venues portfolio in Australia, adding a new facility on the Gold Coast.

Announced this week, Surfers Music Hall will be a 2,500-capacity live music space in Surfers Paradise, the hometown of chart-topping pop star Amy Shark , with a target to open its doors in mid-2028.

Surfers Music Hall will be the concerts giant’s first venue on the Gold Coast, and the first dedicated live music venue of this scale in the region. When complete, the space will bring more national and international tours to the Gold Coast, the second biggest city in Queensland, “while giving local artists a new stage,” reads a statement. Bookings will be open “to a range of promoters,” the message continues. Related Chris Brown Agrees to Increase Child Support -- For Now -- to Ex Diamond in Bitter Custody Fight Bill Donahue

The timing of the new venue is critical. Queensland’s music and entertainment communities are preparing for the opportunity of a lifetime, when Brisbane hosts the 2032 Summer Olympic Games and Paralympic Games. The Gold Coast, about 50 miles south of Brisbane, won’t miss out. Hockey, triathlon, marathon swimming, and basketball games are earmarked for the city.

The buzz is building for the local music scene, too, which has hosted concerts from the likes of Pearl Jam, Foo Fighters and Queen at Carrara Stadium. Also, Live Nation and the City of Gold Coast hosted a Ones to Watch showcase in 2022, and the 2026 Queensland Music Awards (QMAs) were presented on the Gold Coast for the first time in the event’s 20-year history.

Surfers Music Hall will be owned by The City of Gold Coast and operated by Live Nation, and is located within the former Surfers Paradise Transit Centre and Bruce Bishop Carpark precinct. The development, according to LN, is expected to contribute an average of A$20 million ($13 million) each year to the local economy, support some 100 ongoing jobs and create jobs for the creative industries.

As previously reported, Live Nation, OVG and Plenary have been green-lit to build the Gather Brisbane arena ahead of the Games, a 17,000-plus capacity facility that will make the Sunshine State’s capital a two-arena town.

Currently, LN operates the Fortitude Music Hall (3,000) and The Triffid (800) in Brisbane, and boasts a national network of sites, including The Palais Theatre (2,900 capacity) and Festival Hall in Melbourne; Hindley Street Music Hall in Adelaide (1,800), Anita’s Theatre in Wollongong (1,200); and the 13,000-capacity Spark Arena in Auckland, New Zealand.

“They’re substantial… I think it’s like quarterly,” she said, noting that while some residual checks for other projects might be a few cents or dollars, the ones for Full House are “still substantial.” Related Stories Lifestyle Dave Coulier Says Cancer Treatment Has Led to Changes in His Speech and Physical Appearance Movies Why Candace Cameron Bure Says Horror Films Can Lead to a "Portal" That's "Incredibly Demonic"

“I’m always happy when I open that check and deposit it,” Bure added.

So, sometimes you’re like, ‘Oh, cool. That was nice.’ And then sometimes you’re like, ‘All right, well, there’s a nice dinner out.'”

In response, Bure told McBride, “I actually saw that and she said she doesn’t get much now. And I was like, ‘Jodie, you gotta check with your agent or you gotta call your bank,’ ’cause I still get residuals.”

entertainment.body:
Miranda Lambert gave Texans some homestyle country cooking Thursday night (Nov. 26), when she headlined the halftime spot in the NFL Thanksgiving contest between Dallas Cowboys and the visiting Philadelphia Eagles. Explore Miranda Lambert See latest videos, charts and news

Wearing a black cowboy hat and a little black dress emblazoned with stars and finished with long, tasseled sleeves, Lambert delivered a nearly seven-minute medley — with support from the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, a full band and a strings section. The three-time Grammy Award-winning star kicked things off with “Snakeskin Boots,” and got cooking with “Kerosene,” “Gunpowder & Lead,” “Mama’s Broken Heart,” and a cover of Audra Mae and The Almighty Sound’s “Little Red Wagon.”

“Happy Thanksgiving y’all, we love you Texas,” she said at the close.

Lambert has been on a tear of late. Just last week, she was the big winner at the 60th annual Country Music Awards, where she collected three trophies. With that hattrick, she lifted her career total of wins to 17, extending her lead as the female artist with the most victories.

The Longview, TX native ushered in her new album, Crisco , with a set Oct. 1 at the newly-opened Nashville venue The Truth, then dropped her Songline album on Nov. 13, followed by the companion film Songline on Nov. 20, both via Amazon Music.

Also, Lambert co-wrote Ella Langley’ s Billboard Hot 100 smash hit “Choosin’ Texas,” which is now the longest-charting No. 1 in Hot 100 history, with 29 weeks atop the leaderboard. In recent days, “Choosin’ Texas” logged a 50th week atop Billboard ’s Hot Country Songs chart (dated Nov. 28), equaling the all-time mark set by Bebe Rexha and Florida Georgia Line ’s “Meant To Be” in 2017-18.

Unfortunately for the home fans at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, TX, Lambert’s halftime spot was the only highlight. The Eagles defeated the Cowboys 39–38, after being down by as much as 21 points in the third-quarter. Eagles kicker Jake Elliott had the dagger, nailing a game-winning field goal with just two seconds on the clock.

entertainment.title: It’s a Shaolin Thanksgiving! Wu-Tang Clan, Chad Smith Light Up Halftime at Detroit Lions NFL Game
entertainment.summary: The hip-hop legends hit a nearly seven-minute tag-team medley of greatest hits that was announced as “the wrap-up” of its Wu-Tang Forever: The Final Chamber farewell tour.
entertainment.body:
Wu-Tang Clan created a Shaolin Thanksgiving experience in Detroit on Thursday afternoon (Nov. 26), joined by Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer — and homeboy — Chad Smith for a halftime performance at Ford Field for the Lions’ annual Thanksgiving game.

The collective — recently inducted into the Rock And Roll Hall of Fame — lit up the stadium with a nearly seven-minute tag-team medley of greatest hits that was announced as “the wrap-up” of its Wu-Tang Forever: The Final Chamber farewell tour .

Flanked by flags bearing the Wu-Tang and Lions logos, and with 500 fan volunteers moshing on the field in front of the stage and on its wings, the nine surviving MCs — plus Young Dirty Bastard in place of his late father Ol’ Dirty Bastard and DJ Mathematics — kicked off with “Triumph,” then rolled through bits of “4th Chamber,” “Da Mystery of Chessboxin’,” “Protect Ya Neck,” “Method Man,” “Shimmy Shimmy Ya,” “Ice Cream” and “C.R.E.A.M.” The RZA-led “Wu-Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit” finished the set with the group members on the field amidst the fans, with smoke jets shooting up from the stage.

The Lions cheerleading squad also took part in the show, sporting T-shirts with a glittering Wu-Tang/Lions mash-up logo.

“Who’s got it better than me?” Smith — who participated in a 2025 remix of “Wu-Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing Ta F’ Wit” — enthused to Billboard during rehearsals at the stadium on Wednesday. “This is the…Wu-Tang Clan. It’s the halftime show, the biggest game of the year, and the Lions. I’m in my home town, and I get to play drums at halftime with the legendary Wu-Tang — come on! I’m the queen of the ball. And I love those guys. I mean, as far as iconic ’90s hip-hop goes, there’s Nas, maybe, but I love Wu-Tang.”

The Wu-Tang booking was also a personal pleasure for Lions general manager Brad Holmes , an unabashed fanboy who attended the rehearsal as well as the game.

“I would put myself in the die-hard category,” said Holmes, who became a Wu-Tang fan while growing up in Tampa, Fla., and even met U-God after “stalking” the troupe at its hotel before a concert there. “Their music, it really just hit my soul. It’s truly art; I didn’t know how much art it really was, and as I’ve gotten older, the more I listen to it, it just gets even better. When they said Wu-Tang Clan on Thanksgiving, I just” (makes gesture of head exploding).

The Detroit Thanksgiving show — one of three on Thursday, plus U2’s performance on Wednesday night in Los Angeles — was the second of a three-year deal between the Lions with Eminem and his manager and Shady Records President Paul Rosenberg. (Jesse Collins Entertainment stages the show.) Last year’s inaugural installment set a high mark, with Eminem joining fellow home town hero Jack White on stage before a TV audience of nearly 48 million, and Rosenberg said they knew there was a lot to live up to when they began planning this year’s halftime show during spring.

entertainment.title: Robert Pattinson's First Television Role Was In A TV Movie With Alicia Witt And Julian Sands
entertainment.summary: Before Twilight and The Batman, Robert Pattinson made his TV debut in a 2004 fantasy movie alongside Julian Sands, Alicia Witt, and Max von Sydow.
entertainment.body:
In 2004, a fresh-faced Pattinson could be seen making his debut in "Ring of the Nibelungs," a TV fantasy movie based on Norse mythology. Depending on where in the world you were watching and which cut of the film you caught, you might have seen the movie under another title. At one point in the U.S., it was called "Dark Kingdom: The Dragon King," in Germany it was both "The Ring" and "Kingdom in Twilight," in the U.K. it was "Sword of Xanten," and in several countries it was "Curse of the Ring."

That last title featured on promotional posters with a design strongly resembling the title card for the "Lord of the Rings" movies, though not without justification. As the movie's logline proudly declared, "Ring of the Nibelungs" was based on the same legend that inspired Tolkien's novels . The movie featured the heroic Siegfried slaying a dragon for its cursed treasure hoard. Pattinson appeared in a small role as Giselher, ally of Siegfried and brother to Gunther, King of Burgund.

Tandem Productions With a 6.6 IMDb rating and a 63% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, "Ring of the Nibelungs" can hardly be called a roaring success, though there is some appreciation for the early 2000s fantasy film. Robert Pattinson was, at least, in good company in the film. "Ring of the Nibelungs" also starred Julian Sands, known for his roles in 1986's "A Room with a View" and 1991's "Naked Lunch," as well as Alicia Witt and Max von Sydow, both of whom appeared in David Lynch's 1984 adaptation of "Dune."

Following "Ring of the Nibelungs," Pattinson's next credit was as Cedric Diggory in the markedly more successful "Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire." After appearing in the Harry Potter franchise, which is now set for a TV reboot on HBO Max , Pattinson starred in another two TV movies: "The Haunted Airman," in which he again shared the screen with Sands, and the 2007 comedy drama "The Bad Mother's Handbook." The following year, Pattinson landed the role that truly launched his career, Edward Cullen in the vampire romance "Twilight."

After the Twilight Saga concluded, Pattinson underwent something of a reinvention, taking on darker dramas, including "Good Time," "The Lighthouse," and "Mickey 17." These, along with appearances in Christopher Nolan's "Tenet" and "The Odyssey," have proven Pattinson has the dramatic chops required to take on the legendary role of James Bond.

There's certainly a high chance you've heard a family member make that infamous request once everyone has gathered around the table for Thanksgiving , a time filled with aforementioned turkey and stuffing yourself with the requisite mashed potatoes, pumpkin pie and a whole lot of awkward small talk with those distant family members you see about as often as you go to the dentist.

"I know, I can't believe it's been so long." "Yes, I'm still single." "No, I haven't watched The Studio yet."

And that's why you need comfort food. No, we're not talking about Aunt Maureen's green bean casserole and the rest of the feast you're impatiently waiting to dive into, we're talking about comfort food for your soul that only a treasured TV show or movie can provide.

So if you're looking for a cozy distraction right now, we've rounded up some of our favorite Thanksgiving-themed episodes of shows like Gossip Girl , How I Met Your Mother and Friends (could the NBC series be any better at celebrating the football-and feast-focused holiday), as well as a few movies about Turkey Day.

Yes, there are actually plenty of films made about the Jan Brady of holidays, even if Halloween and Christmas tend to gobble up the majority of the attention at the end of each year.

Some are more showy about it (see: Planes, Trains & Automobiles ) while others just make a passing reference, but thanks to that scene in Zabar's (featuring a pre- Grey's Anatomy Sara Ramirez ) we want You've Got Mail to be a Thanksgiving movie, we want it so badly.

So, stockpile a plate of leftovers, hibernate in the basement and get ready to stream your long weekend away.

entertainment.title: The Hunting Wives Creator Defends Major Season 2 Death: 'It's Important That Things Have Consequences'
entertainment.summary: The second season of Netflix's The Hunting Wives loses a major character in Episode 5. Creator Rebecca Perry Sutter tells TVLine why it had to happen.
entertainment.body:
Netflix Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Warning: This interview spoils a major twist from "The Hunting Wives" Season 2, Episode 6. Proceed at your own risk.

Now streaming on Netflix, the second season of "The Hunting Wives" takes the ladies Maple Brook, Texas on another deadly thrill ride — and not everyone makes it out alive. The biggest death of the season, and arguably the series, occurs in Episode 6. It's shocking, it's upsetting, and like most tragedies on this show, it involves Margo.

Malin Akerman's character returns home from a chaotic church service, only to find Brad waiting in her living room. She knows that he's unwell — the entire congregation watched him interrupt the service in a hospital gown, begging his father for help — but she doesn't know exactly what went down behind closed church doors, including that Brad shot his father for picking up the police's phone call.

Brad puts down the gun long enough to have a civilized catch-up with his former lover, but that doesn't mean Margo likes what she hears. New information has Brad questioning whether his mother really killed Abby last season, and when when he remembers hearing Margo mention an abortion, he puts two and two together, concluding that Margo is the killer.

In a very "Chicago" moment, both Margo and Brad reach for the gun, but Margo gets her hands on it first, shooting Brad dead in her own home. Naturally, Sophie comes to Margo's rescue, agreeing to tell the police that Brad was shot in self-defense.

"R.I.P., Baby Brad!" series creator Rebecca Perry Cutter tells TVLine, explaining that she wrote Brad's dramatic downfall in Season 2 because she knew that actor George Ferrier "could do more than he did in Season 1," which he absolutely proved in these six episodes.

And while many viewers are likely disappointed to lose this lovable mess, Cutter believes that Brad's death was a necessary road bump in the Hunting Wives' collective journey .

"I think it's important that things have consequences," Cutter says. "He is kind of the biggest living victim of Season 1 because his girlfriend was murdered, and his mom was murdered and blamed for being a murderer. Margo did this to him, so I think it was important to let the reality of that exist. We wanted to show that, yeah, he got f***king traumatized, and then his father can't deal with him, and he's shipped away, and s**t goes bad. That was just something that we were really interested in seeing."

Beloved local grocer Zingone Bros. on Manhattan’s Upper West Side is closing after nearly 100 years , leaving its famed bodega cat Oliver, who starred in an Olivia Rodrigo music video, looking for a new home.

entertainment.title: Steelers owner picks a side in Aaron Rodgers and coach Mike McCarthy’s nasty public feud
entertainment.summary: The team owner said it was the right move to cut Rodgers after his recent "insubordination."
entertainment.body:
It’s safe to say Aaron Rodgers won’t be getting a gift from his former boss this holiday season.

Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II made it crystal clear that he’s in Mike McCarthy’s corner amid the head coach’s explosive feud with the quarterback — saying Rodgers’ actions this week were out of bounds.

“I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette .

“The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization,” he continued. “When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.”

Rodgers — who previously stated this would be his final NFL season — was cut by the Steelers Wednesday, shortly after he gave a jaw-dropping assessment of his reunion with McCarthy on the “Pat McAfee Show.”

During the interview, Rodgers claimed the coach — with whom he won a Super Bowl as a member of the Green Bay Packers in 2011 — was falling asleep during meetings, was “unhealthy” and broke a huddle by saying the wrong team’s name .

McCarthy later claimed Rodgers presented an ultimatum over play-calling duties , telling him to either hand the reins to someone else or release him.

Rodgers’ appearance on the ESPN show came after he found out through teammate Pat Freiermuth that he lost his starting gig to backup quarterback Mason Rudolph. His words have since been slammed by many, including his former Packers teammate T.J. Lang .

entertainment.title: Anuel AA’s ‘RHLM2’ Album Is Finally Here: ‘I Made It With My Heart and Soul’
entertainment.summary: The long-awaited album is a sequel to his 2018 debut, Real Hasta La Muerte, and his first in four years.
entertainment.body:
Anuel AA is celebrating his 34th birthday on Thursday (Nov. 26) with the release of his long-awaited RHLM2 album.

The sequel to his debut studio album, Real Hasta La Muerte (2018), is home to 23 tracks that blend trap and reggaetón. It’s a return to the sound that made him a household name as “El Dios del Trap” (The God of Latin Trap).

Though it’s taken the Puerto Rican act nearly 10 years to release the sequel to RHLM — which debuted at No. 1 on Top Latin Albums in July 2018—he has released other promising albums in between, including Emmanuel (2020) and Las Leyendas Nunca Mueren (2021), both of which also hit No. 1 on the chart.

“I poured my heart and soul into this album for everyone who believes in me and stays loyal no matter what. This album means the world to me. There are no perfect words to explain how I feel and what I feel for this album,” he said in an Instagram post ahead of the set’s release on Thanksgiving night. He dedicated his new project to his fans, his family and those who have stuck by his side during the good and bad times.

He continued: “Thank you for never giving up on me, I love you all so much with all my heart!!!!!!! I made this album for you […] I will never forget you!!!!!”

From trapsoul to sensual reggaetón, RHLM2 includes fiery collaborations such as “Sexo Nama” with De La Rose, “Tal Ve Un Ignorante Fui” with ROA and “Si Me Matan a Balazos” with Fuerza Regida. Most notable is “Instagram,” a collaboration with Blessd and Wisin, where they cleverly sample Don Omar’s 2006 hit “Myspace” alongside Wisin y Yandel.

The set wraps with five previously released commercial hits—“Amanece” feat. Haze (2018), “Mas Rica Que Ayer” feat. Mambo Kingz & DJ Luian (2022), “¿Qué Nos Pasó?” (2022), “La Llevo al Cielo” feat. Chris Jedi, Chencho Corleone & Ñengo Flow (2022) and the Ovy on the Drums-produced “Deportivo” feat. Blessd (2024)—further reminding fans of his ongoing star power.

entertainment.title: Watch Miranda Lambert Perform Medley of Her Hits at Dallas Cowboys Halftime Show
entertainment.summary: The native Texan tackled songs like "Gunpowder & Lead" and "Little Red Wagon" in her first NFL appearance during the annual Thanksgiving tradition

Singing a medley of her classic hits (which she affectionately called “bangers and mash,” i.e., a mashup of her bangers), Lambert made her halftime show debut during the Thanksgiving Day matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium.

Following a pretaped introduction by Reba McEntire, who announced Lambert as the “most awarded artist in the history of the Academy of Country Music,” the Grammy-winning singer took the stage to perform “Snakeskin Boots” (sorry, no Ella Langley cameo), “Kerosene,” “Gunpowder & Lead,” “Mama’s Broken Heart,” and “Little Red Wagon.” Lambert was backed by her band, along with a string section wearing black cowboy hats to mirror that of the entertainer: Lambert, in a black hat, wore a black dress adorned with blue fames. She also received an assist from an army of Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, who delivered their choreographed routine as Lambert sang.

entertainment.summary: Paige DeSorbo is serving up a hard launch. Four months after the Summer House alum denied rumors that she and boyfriend Joe D’Amelio got engaged, she made their romance social media official,...
entertainment.body:
Four months after the Summer House alum denied rumors that she and boyfriend Joe D’Amelio got engaged, she made their romance social media official, sharing a funny video on TikTok of her friends making homemade pizzas.

As DeSorbo captioned the Nov. 25 TikTok video, which she also shared on her Instagram Stories, “We aren’t Italian at all.”

The clip featured the Giggly Squad podcast host’s pals cooking up pies and hanging out as they lip-synced to audio from a scene from the 1990 classic Goodfellas , in which Henry Hill ( Ray Liotta ) introduces the members of mafia capo Paulie Cicero ’s crew.

“There was Jimmy, and Tommy, and me. And there was Anthony Stabile, Frankie Carbone,” Liotta’s Hill says in the scene. “And then there was Mo Black’s brother, Fat Andy and his guys, Frankie the Wop and Freddy No Nose. And then there was Pete the Killer, who was Sally Balls’ brother. Then you had Nickey Eyes and Mikey Franzese.”

And among the family and friends who made a cameo in DeSorbo’s video was D’Amelio, who lifted up his drink in greeting as the camera panned to him during the “Nickey Eyes” line.

While the couple first sparked romance rumors way back in February 2025, they have kept their relationship offline until now. And fans couldn’t help but get excited about the update.

“GIRRRRRRRRL it’s tiktok official okayyy honey,” one user wrote in the comments section of DeSorbo’s video, while another added, “Paige he’s so handsome and fits in so well I’m so happy for you kween.”

Although this marks the D’Amelio’s debut on DeSorbo’s social media, the Bravo alum previously shared insight into their romance, joking to Us Weekly in a February interview that while Italian men have a reputation for being “not quiet,” she’s found that’s not the case.

entertainment.title: Lana Del Rey Says New Albums Are ‘Getting Close’ to Completion: ‘I’m Happy With Them’
entertainment.summary: The singer-songwriter updated fans on Stove and its companion album, Spyda , while seemingly teasing cryptic lyrics.
entertainment.body:
Lana Del Rey is giving fans an update on her long-awaited new music.

In a Thanksgiving Day Instagram post on Thursday (Nov. 26), the alt-pop singer-songwriter revealed that her upcoming country album, Stove , and its companion album, Spyda , are “definitely getting close to wrapping up.”

“The albums are coming along so well. I’m happy with them,” Del Rey wrote alongside a photo gallery. “Taking time cooking but definitely gonna be out at the perfect time considering how much music is on both of them. Definitely getting close to wrapping up although did take so many unexpected turns over the years. Can’t say I saw it coming but what came out of it feels meant to be — it makes me wonder where I would even go after this.”

Although Del Rey didn’t reveal a release date for either project, she offered insight into the albums’ evolution.

“It’s an unusual coupling of albums that explain where I started when I announced everything 4 years ago to my perspective now on my internal web of people and their reactions to my happiness and physical growth and success,” she wrote.

Del Rey also offered insight into the albums’ introspective themes, referencing what may be a song titled “You’ve Got a Friend.” She described its lyrics as containing substantial “internal dialogue” about the events of the past several years, the lessons she’s learned, and whether everything happens on “God’s time.”

“Makes me feel like there’s no way the things that happen could be random – one thing that comes to mind is that little quote… You can have it all, but you can’t have it all at the same time,” she wrote.

The “Summertime Sadness” singer also revealed that the physical editions will be an important part of the projects.

entertainment.title: The Hunting Wives' Exciting New Couple Wasn't Part Of The Plan For Season 2, EP Says: 'But Once I Saw The Chemistry...'
entertainment.summary: A new couple emerges in Season 2 of The Hunting Wives, even if the Netflix drama's creator tells TVLine it wasn't part of her original plan.
entertainment.body:
Netflix Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Warning: This article spoils Season 2, Episode 5 of Netflix's "The Hunting Wives." Proceed with caution.

Released on Thanksgiving, the second season of Netflix's "The Hunting Wives" gives patient fans plenty to be thankful for, with more twists, more turns, and, of course, more pegging. For now, we're specifically raising our glass to a juicy reveal in Episode 5, confirming that two beloved characters are even more fond of each other than the fans are of them.

We're talking, of course, about Deputy Wanda Salazar (Karen Rodriguez) and Deputy Walter Flynn (Hunter Emery), both of whom were promoted to series regulars for Season 2. We learn through a flashback in Episode 5 that Flynn and Salazar have been secretly hooking up for at least two months, much to the delight of their shippers.

"It's so funny, my original pitch for Season 2 to Netflix was that we would reveal that [Flynn and Salazar] had slept together, but they would not end up together because she's the only character in the show that puts her job first and has a real moral compass," series creator Rebecca Perry Cutter tells TVLine. "But once I saw the chemistry, I was like, no, f*** that."

And thank goodness Cutter decided against her original plan, because Flynn and Salazar's romance provides a much-needed bright spot in a season otherwise jam-packed with death, deceit, and general devastation. She sits by his side when a shoot-out with Zelda's thugs leaves him comatose, and he stands by her side at the end of the season when... well, we won't give that away for those who haven't finished their binge yet.

Netflix But as much as Rebecca Perry Cutter loves the relationship that Flynn and Salazar bring to "The Hunting Wives" Season 2 , they aren't her favorite couple on the Netflix drama. No, that honor — as surprising as it may sound to some readers — goes to Callie (Jaime Ray Newman) and Sheriff Jonny (Branton Box), both of whom engage in quite a bit of extramarital fun this year.

"I still maintain that Callie and Jonny have the best marriage on the show," Cutter tells TVLine. "The joy about doing this show, about sexuality and queer sexuality in this repressed red town, is that we don't have to define things the way you would define them in the big city. So I don't know, what does he call himself? I don't get to decide that. It's sort of mystery, and I love the mystery of it, and I love Callie and Johnny together."

entertainment.body:
After the Dancing With the Stars cohost made waves for her fashion choices during season 35, she shed insight into her looks while responding to those who gave a low score on her style.

“I really feel like I’m at this next inflection of my career,” Hough told Glamour in an interview published Nov. 24 alongside her stylist Brad Goreski . “When you get into your late 30s, you just don’t give a f--k anymore. You’re like, ‘Who am I? What do I want to wear? What makes me feel incredible?’ It has more intention rather than trying to fit into what’s hot.”

“I feel like I’m in my leading lady era,” she continued. “I mean that in the actual projects that I’m doing, but also me as a person.”

To cohost this season of DWTS alongside Alfonso Ribeiro , the professional dancer decided to take a step out of her usual style comfort zone.

“I’ve gone a little bit more vixen-y this year than I have girl next door because we’re trying to find that character,” she shared. “It’s been very strategic.”

As she twirled with a new vibe, Hough took some fashion risks, including a sultry Valentino ensemble—which featured a skin-colored bodysuit under a see-through skirt—during the Nov. 17 episode that really had fans talking, with one social media user calling for Hough’s stylist to be “fired” in a viral Instagram video .

But as for Goreski, he doesn’t believe the online chatter about Hough’s looks is completely pointe-less anyway, emphasizing that “any conversation, good or bad, around fashion is great.”

“I think Jules ultimately brings the looks to life,” he added, praising his client. “I’m glad that there’s another part of the show that people talk about. Not every person’s going to love every look. I know that from being a stylist for 15 years. And that’s okay.”

entertainment.title: One Actor From The Body Is Also In Josh Hartnett's Nautical Netflix Monster Series
entertainment.summary: From a spooky Catholic school to the farthest reaches of the open ocean, genre television can take you anywhere - something this actor knows all too well.
entertainment.body:
Netflix Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover If you've seen the 2026 psychological teen drama "The Body" on Netflix , you may have noticed a character with a screen presence as impressive as his red beard. Canadian actor Josh Cruddas plays Pastor Caleb, a local religious figure and late father to one of the series protagonists, Lisbeth Anderson (Geena Meszaros). Though he only shows up in five of the show's eight episodes, his presence is one of the driving forces behind Lisbeth's actions.

Cruddas also starred in the Josh Hartnett-led series, "Below," which streamed a month earlier on Netflix. "Below" is a show with Stephen King vibes , centering a remote Newfoundland town where the locals are plagued by a mysterious sea creature. Here, fisherman Calvin Penney (Josh Hartnett) must protect his family from the fallout of the creature's presence. Cruddas appears in four of the eight episodes, playing a loan shark named Connor Kopecko who's out to collect a debt from Calvin's youngest son, Jay Penney (Rohan Campbell).

Cruddas's portrayal of both characters involve some genre bending of horror, mystery, suspense, and comedy. "I'm a little scaredy pants, so my consumption of [genre] content is quite limited," Cruddas told Popternative in October 2026. "I just bring [myself to each role]. I've noticed that I gotta have a schtick sometimes, [but] I hope I'm doing every character justice. I try to bring new stuff, but also, you're gonna get a ginger with a beard, no matter what."

Netflix In addition to "The Body" and "Below," Cruddas has a number of other notable film and TV roles to his name, such as that of Fred Waite in the 2022's true-story Western "Billy the Kid," and Miles Miller in "Revival," another 2025 horror-mystery series that's streaming on Netflix.

Cruddas also makes waves off screen as a decorated coach and teacher in the musical theater space. He has over a decade of coaching experience, which includes a faculty member position at the Musical Arts Academy in Ontario, and he's an in-demand private acting and singing instructor for young kids. He also received a 2019 Best Acting Teacher nomination in the internationally recognized Stagecoach Performing Arts school.

Cruddas has pointed to his theater background and teaching experience as something he's consistently drawn from while acting — not only to make his own screen characters feel distinct, but to help young actors who have aspirations of being in a series one day. "I consider [teaching singing and acting] to be just as rewarding and important as any of the other work I do," he told Close-up in 2019. "I remember how much performing impacted my life for the better as a child and teen, and the people who inspired me. If I can bring even a fraction of that joy to the young folks I teach, I'm happy."

On a rainy day in Buffalo, the fourth quarter featured Bass making a 54-yard field goal to tie the game 10-10, Butker missing a 46-yard field goal that would have given the lead back to the Chiefs, and then Bass making a 57-yard field goal as time expired to win the game, 13-10.

Bass has been excellent this season. He’s now 26-for-27 on field goals in 2026, with his only miss coming from 54 yards in last week’s win over the Dolphins.

Butker has been terrible this season. He’s now 15-for-23 on field goals in 2026, and his eight misses are the most for any kicker in the league. He also hasn’t made a single kick longer than 50 yards this season; 31 other NFL kickers have made at least one from beyond 50.

Chiefs coach Andy Reid said after the loss that he wasn’t ready to say whether Butker will remain the kicker in Kansas City.

“I’ll go back and go through all of it again,” Reid said immediately after the game. “Not gonna make any decisions right this minute.”

It’s hard to see how the Chiefs can stick with Butker down the stretch. A kicker’s job is to make his kicks, and Butker simply isn’t performing.

sports.title: Andy Reid: New York overturned Rashee Rice catch, not a call I agree with
sports.summary: The most pivotal call on Thanksgiving night was a replay review that went against the Chiefs.
sports.body:
With the Chiefs facing third-and-10 at their own 9-yard line with 1:51 remaining in the fourth quarter, Patrick Mahomes hit Rashee Rice over the middle for what the officials ruled was a sensational 11-yard catch. But the officiating office reviewed the play and ruled that Rice lost control as he was going to the ground. Reid said after the game that the on-field officials told him they thought it was a catch but the officiating office overruled them. Reid agreed with the officials on the field.

“Not one that I agreed with, but they said it came from New York,” Reid said. “It’s not from these guys, our guys called it a completion — the guys who were working the game. I’m not sure what they saw. I saw he had control of the ball, then his elbow hit, then the ball hit, but he had control. Normally, in those kind of situations, it’s got to be clear and obvious. And to me, that was not clear and obvious.”

It was a big play, as it went from the Chiefs having first-and-10 at the 20-yard line with all three timeouts and a real chance of driving for a game-winning score on that possession, to the Chiefs having fourth-and-10 at their own 9-yard line and punting the ball back to the Bills. Ultimately, after an exchange of punts, it was the Bills who kicked the game-winning field goal as time expired. And it was Reid left to wonder what might have been if the call on the field had stood.

Cris Collinsworth talked about the laces on the ball, and when Rice hit the ground his hand moved down those laces while the ball touched the turf. I think it’s pretty clear the ball moved. sports.title: Tyler Bass hits walk-off 57-yard field goal, Bills beat Chiefs 13-10
sports.summary: Buffalo overcame some nasty weather to once again defeat Kansas City in the regular season.
sports.body:
Buffalo’s kicker sent a walk-off, 57-yard field goal through the uprights to give the Bills a 13-10 victory over the Chiefs, putting the club further in the driver’s seat for the AFC’s No. 1 seed.

The game was not without controversy, particularly late in the contest. But the weather conditions also affected both teams, as neither offense got much going.

Josh Allen finished the game 10-of-21 for 81 yards with two interceptions, rushing for 43 yards on seven attempts. Allen’s passer rating of 18.3 is the second lowest of his career in any regular-season game.

Patrick Mahomes completed 16-of-29 passes for 174 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions.

James Cook ended up pacing the offense for Buffalo, rushing for 117 yards on 32 carries with Buffalo’s only touchdown — a 5-yard run in the second quarter.

The Chiefs got a 26-yard field goal from Harrison Butker to close the first half and a 1-yard touchdown from Emmett Johnson to open the second half. But the team was not able to score again.

After Bass connected on a 54-yard field goal in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 10-10, Butker missed his eighth field goal of the year — this one going wide right from 46 yards out.

Kansas City had the ball with another shot to get Butker in field goal range. But what looked like a third-down completion from Mahomes to Rahsee Rice was overturned on replay, allowing Buffalo to field another punt.

sports.body: I picked a bad day to stop sniffing glue. The Buffalo Bills and the Kansas City Chiefs have played plenty of classics over the course of the last decade. It’s been a while since we had a true terrible weather game between these two clubs, and while it might have kept the scoring down from what we would otherwise have expected, the bad weather certainly didn’t lessen the intensity of the game. Buffalo jumped out to a 7-0 lead early, but a red zone turnover kept the Bills from adding to their lead. Kansas City logged their first points in a two-minute drill to close out the first half, and they scored again coming out of the half to give them a 10-7 lead. That score stayed put for a long time. Tyler Bass drilled a 54-yard kick in the fourth quarter to tie. And then, he hit another bomb, this time from 57 yards out, to secure a hard-fought, 13-10 victory. I need a cigarette, and I don’t even smoke. Whereas Kansas City punter Matt Araiza struggled with the weather, uncorking a short punt before he dropped another snap and netted just eight yards on his second attempt, Doman pinned the Chiefs deep with his second attempt, which gave the Bills good field position after they forced a punt. Doman hit a boomer heading into the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter, pinning the Chiefs at the 13-yard line. sports.body: Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau moved into a tie for seventh place on the team’s all-time sacks list on Thanksgiving night. Rousseau sacked quarterback Patrick Mahomes on a 3rd & 16 midway through the third quarter on Thanksgiving night to bring his career total to 43, catching former Bills defensive end Mario Williams. [Media: https://twitter.com/NFL/status/2126156691347808404?a=4Khc_jbNIPbmkep54LM&s=20] Williams spent four seasons (2012-2015) in Buffalo, recording double-digit sacks in each of his first three years with the team. His best season came in 2014 when he recorded 14.5 sacks and earned first-team All-Pro honors. Rousseau, now in his sixth NFL season, has spent his entire career in Buffalo after the Bills selected him with the 30th overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft. Having already established a new personal single-season record for sacks this year, the 26 year old is now working his way through some familiar names in Buffalo’s history books. Once Rousseau gets past Mario Williams, there’s another Williams waiting for him. Former defensive tackle Kyle Williams (48.5), who spent all 13 of his NFL seasons in Buffalo, sits sixth on the franchise’s all-time list. With six regular-season games remaining, and the way Rousseau has been getting to opposing quarterbacks lately, we might not have to wait until next season to talk about him catching another Williams.

sports.summary: Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III has a share of another NFL record. Cook has now rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in 10 consecutive games, tying a record Terry Allen set across the 1995 and 1996 seasons with Washington. Cook found the end zone against the Kansas City Chiefs on [
sports.body: Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III has a share of another NFL record. Cook has now rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in 10 consecutive games, tying a record Terry Allen set across the 1995 and 1996 seasons with Washington. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2126154593432178811?a=1zaXZ7gEe8A1q0j_ZqM&s=20] Cook found the end zone against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night during the second quarter to put the Bills up 7-0. He then eclipsed the 75-yard mark in the third quarter on a five-yard run that put him at 79 for the night. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2126135452583252133?a=kUYUD6G_ydbk91qANxM&s=20] It’s been 30 years since Allen put together his streak of 10 games. Since then, we’ve watched some pretty impressive running backs come through the NFL. LaDainian Tomlinson, Adrian Peterson, and Derrick Henry have all had their share of record-setting performances, but none of them managed to do what Cook just did. And unlike Allen, who needed parts of two seasons to put together his streak, Cook has done it all in the same season. In fact, the Bills’ season opener was the only game this year in which Cook didn’t meet both statistical requirements. Cook entered Thursday night’s game having rushed for 1,003 yards and 10 touchdowns over the course of his nine-game streak, averaging 111.4 yards per game and 5.1 yards per carry. He eclipsed the century mark in five of those nine games, including a season-high 157-yard performance against the New York Jets. Remember when we spent so much of the offseason in 2025 talking about whether the Bills should pay Cook? Buffalo eventually gave its running back a four-year, $48 million contract extension, and Cook has spent the better part of two seasons giving us reasons to talk about what a good decision that was. The Bills will head to Foxborough next week for their second meeting of the season with the New England Patriots. Cook rushed for 75 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in their first matchup. Another 75 yards and a trip to the end zone next week, and Cook will have an NFL record all to himself. Considering we’ve been watching him do just that every week since September, it might be time to start wondering just how big a number he’s going to leave for the next running back to chase.

sports.title: Jerry Jones on Mike McCarthy: "He was outstanding as the head coach"
sports.summary: The recent remarks from former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers regarding Steelers coach Mike McCarthy have raised plenty of questions, posed to plenty of people.
sports.body:
After Thursday’s 39-38 loss to the Eagles, Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones was asked about McCarthy, who coached Jones’s team for five seasons, from 2020 through 2024.

“I offered him to stay at least another year when he left,” Jones told reporters. “And so I thought he was outstanding as the head coach and had a great command of, frankly, quarterback, offense. Can’t say enough good things about him. He’s, frankly, one of the finest people that around football that I’ve been around. And I can’t say enough about him. I never had the type of thing that is being said about him. I never had that in consideration in any of my time with him, extending his contract. Any of that, that was never on the table. And we never had an issue within the organization.”

That conflicts, obviously, with the things Rodgers said on Wednesday.

Regardless, Jones no longer employs McCarthy. While Jones possibly chose to take the high road, a former employer vouching for a coach is fundamentally different than his current employer vouching for him.

McCarthy took the Cowboys to the playoffs three times in five years, advancing to the divisional round in 2022. The Cowboys failed to qualify for the postseason in the first year after McCarthy left. Thursday’s loss to the Eagles makes it harder for them to get there the second post-McCarthy season.

sports.title: Mike Tomlin on current Steelers situation: "It's a dumpster fire"
sports.summary: Former Steelers coach speaks at length about this week's events.
sports.body:
Appearing on NBC’s Chiefs-Bills halftime show on Thanksgiving night, Tomlin shared his thoughts on the situation in a conversation with Mike Tirico. (A portion of it was on the live broadcast; the full interview is here .)

“I had a range of emotions watching those course of events yesterday,” Tomlin told Tirico. “I think the prevailing one is just general sadness. Sad on a micro level, sad on a macro level. And by that, I mean, you know, just from an individual perspective, sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career of the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, and just on the macro level, whether it’s organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum.

“Those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football. So, just a lot of emotions, but probably more than anything, man, general sadness on a lot of levels.”

Tirico asked Tomlin if he was shocked by Rodgers’s decision to air dirty laundry in a public forum.

“It certainly did,” Tomlin said, “but, you know, and particularly because I know both men involved, certainly had a lot of intimate work and development of relationship with Aaron over the last couple of years, and have known and competed against Mike, you know, respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time. But I don’t — what I acknowledge is I don’t know them as a collective, the nature of their relationships, and so certainly I was surprised by that.”

Regardless of Rodgers’s conduct on the way out the door, Tomlin explained that Rodgers was viewed favorably by his teammates in 2025.

“He was beloved, and I’m not, you know, over-exaggerating that,” Tomlin said. “He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture, to be engaged with teammates, and particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process, or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, et cetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real, natural way. He was a tireless worker regarding the process.

“I called early-morning quarterback meetings on Wednesday and Thursday. He was always early and engaged. Did a heck of a job in terms of engaging and developing, assisting in the development of young players. Specifically, Will Howard was always in that meeting, and, shoot, man, [Rodgers] and I were shoulder-to-shoulder in terms of the development of Will and challenging Will to develop professional habits. And so, you know, it was early and extremely consistent during my time with him, in terms of his willingness to work in those areas, and I think that’s why he’s so beloved in that locker room, as been reported by multiple sources in light of this incident. That is real. The guys in that locker room love and appreciate Aaron Rodgers.”

sports.title: Bills lead Chiefs 7-3 at halftime on Thanksgiving night
sports.summary: Nasty weather in Western New York has limited offensive production for both Buffalo and Kansas City.
sports.body:
With steady freezing rain falling throughout the first half, it was difficult for both teams to get much going offensively. The game-time temperature was 35 degrees but the feels like temperature was down to 21.

The Bills have relied on running back James Cook for most of their offensive production. Cook rushed for 71 yards on 19 carries in the first half with a 5-yard touchdown.

Josh Allen is just 5-of-10 passing for 41 yards with an interception. Safety Alohi Gilman picked off Allen in the end zone on second-and-8 from the Kansas City 9 midway through the second quarter. At that point, it seemed like if the Bills scored a touchdown, they might have an insurmountable lead.

While the Chiefs didn’t score off of that interception, they at least kept Buffalo off the board.

But Kansas City had several miscues from the wet ball. The team had trouble fielding kicks, punter Matt Ariza had trouble catching a long snap before a punt, and Patrick Mahomes had trouble fielding a snap.

But Kansas City finally got a little something going late in the second quarter, with Harrison Butker sending a 26-yard field goal through the uprights to narrow Buffalo’s lead to four points.

Through 30 minutes, Mahomes is 10-of-15 for 97 yards. Travis Kelce has four receptions for 71 yards, including a key 21-yard catch at the end of the first half to get Kansas City into scoring position.

sports.title: Jeffery Simmons: I didn't simulate snap count on false starts, Lions are "crying" about a them problem
sports.summary: Long before the Bears beat the Lions on a last-second touchdown catch by wide receiver Rome Odunze, one of the storylines of the game was a run of false start penalties by the Lions.
sports.body:
Center Juice Scruggs was called for back-to-back false starts and then picked up a third later in the half. Left guard Christian Mahogany was flagged for another one before the next snap and there were indications from the Lions that Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons was simulating the snap count to get them to jump.

Mahogany made that accusation explicit after the game that the Bears “find out the snap count of the quarterback and they use it” while adding that Lions linemen were wearing microphones that he believes will back him up. Simmons was not penalized, but was seen speaking to the referee during a break in play. He denied Mahogany’s allegation after the 39-35 win.

“We don’t have to . We don’t have to,” Simmons said, via Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press “We line up and play football. They quarterback check. I said, ‘Run.’ I didn’t say, ‘Hut.’ I mean, their cadence, they say, ‘White 80, white 80.’ I mean, when you lose football games, it’s a lot of complaining and a lot of crying. I mean, there was a couple times that they false start, we didn’t say a word. So that’s their problem, not ours. . . . If I say, ‘Run,’ I’m telling my defense, run. Think I care to tell them what they about to do? I’m talking to my guys. So all the crying that they’re doing, that’s a them problem, not me.”

Mahogany was flagged for taunting Simmons during a 70-yard Jahmyr Gibbs touchdown run in the fourth quarter and kicker Jake Bates missed the ensuing extra point to leave the score 35-24. The Lions would not score again and the Bears headed back to Chicago with an improbable victory.

sports.summary: There is some nasty weather in Western New York on Thanksgiving night.

sports.title: Nick Sirianni is pulled away from fans after comeback win
sports.summary: Good or bad, right or wrong, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni has had from time to time the demeanor of a fan who won a contest to be the head coach for a day.
sports.body:
On Thursday in Dallas, he displayed those qualities after a stunning come-from-way-behind win over the Cowboys.

While celebrating the 39-38 win (they trailed 31-10, late in the third quarter), Sirianni approached fans in field-level suites. He eventually had to be pulled away by Dom DiSandro.

It’s unclear whether he was interacting with Cowboys fans or Eagles fans. He appeared to be making an aggressive movement toward someone before DiSandro intervened.

The Eagles contend that Sirianni was celebrating with Eagles fans, and that Sirianni was pulled away so that he could shake the hand of Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer after the game.

There was never any contact (at least none that the cameras captured). Still, it’s a bad look — and it’s definitely on brand.

While Sirianni has yet to cross the line, it seems like he will, one of these days.

Regardless, the Eagles have now won two in a row after losing seven in a row. They’re 4-7 and on the fringes of contention in the NFC East.

sports.title: Eagles mount furious comeback, beat Cowboys 39-38 in Thanksgiving classic
sports.summary: What looked like a blowout turned into a great one, as Philadelphia stormed back to win in Dallas.
sports.body:
In a wild game that went from an apparent blowout to a thrilling comeback, the Cowboys jumped out to a 31-10 lead and then lost 39-38 when Eagles kicker Jake Elliott hit a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left.

Eagles quarterback Joe Milton played by far the best game of his career, throwing for 331 yards, with three touchdown passes and a touchdown run. We’ve always known Milton had a strong arm, but he showed today that he’s more than just a thrower. He can lead an NFL offense as a quarterback.

But Dak Prescott is a good quarterback, too, and he turned in a big game of his own. He threw for 291 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions.

Prescott’s favorite receiver was CeeDee Lamb, who finished with 134 receiving yards, and running back Javonte Williams ran for two touchdowns and also caught a touchdown pass.

The Eagles, however, got a monster game from wide receiver DeVonta Smith, who had 11 catches for 200 yards and two touchdowns. Smith was sensational while the Eagles were coming back in the fourth quarter.

Special teams miscues killed the Cowboys: The Eagles blocked a punt for a touchdown, and Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal in the fourth quarter. Aubrey, who became the highest-paid kicker in the NFL this offseason, is having the worst season of his career.

The loss drops the Cowboys to 5-7 and is devastating to their playoff hopes. The 4-7 Eagles aren’t contenders, but they played like contenders today.

Tight end Dalton Kincaid is active for the Thanksgiving matchup while cornerback Christian Benford is inactive.

Kincaid was listed as questionable with thumb and ankle injuries. He missed Sunday’s win over the Dolphins.

For the Chiefs, Kenneth Walker will miss his third straight game with a groin injury as he was ruled out on Wednesday.

sports.title: Buffalo Bills vs. Kansas City Chiefs, NFL Week 12 Thanksgiving Day fan discussion
sports.summary: Tonight, one of the NFL’s biggest games of the 2026 NFL season plays out in Orchard Park, NY. The Buffalo Bills take on the Kansas City Chiefs tonight for a Thanksgiving Day game in primetime. This is the first time the Bills are hosting a game on Thanksgiving, and it comes against one of their […]
sports.body: Tonight, one of the NFL’s biggest games of the 2026 NFL season plays out in Orchard Park, NY. The Buffalo Bills take on the Kansas City Chiefs tonight for a Thanksgiving Day game in primetime. This is the first time the Bills are hosting a game on Thanksgiving, and it comes against one of their biggest rivals — and what many believe to be the best rivalry in sports today. At 9-1, Buffalo is currently in first place in the AFC and in control of their playoff fate. If the regular season ended today, the Bills would claim the one seed and a bye to begin the postseason. If the current standings prevail, the 8-2 Chiefs would be the five seed, and playing at the Cincinnati Bengals in the Wild Card round. Tonight’s game isn’t isn’t of the elimination variety because there’s a lot more football yet to play, but there’s a lot at stake for both the winner and loser. If Buffalo loses they’d surrender a head-to-head advantage to Kansas City, and sole possession of first place in the conference. While many in Chiefs Kingdom are quick to remind Bills Mafia that regular-season wins don’t really matter, that couldn’t be further from the truth. You can be sure that quarterbacks Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes know how big this game is for their seasons. Will Allen and the Bills take down the Chiefs in head coach Joe Brady’s first matchup leading the team against Andy Reid and Steve Spagnuolo? When Buffalo and Kansas City square off, anything’s possible! However, remember that the weather might have a say in how this one plays out. Here’s your open thread for Bills-Chiefs on Thanksgiving night. As always, be kind to each other — and in all things… go Bills!

sports.title: Penalties and forward progress ruling help Cowboys score before halftime
sports.summary: The Cowboys lead the Eagles 28-10.
sports.body:
The Cowboys’ final drive of the first half was aided by three straight plays: A 10-yard pass interference penalty, a 30-yard pass interference penalty, and a questionable call on which the officials ruled Javonte Williams’ forward progress had stopped before he dropped a ball that Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen picked up and raced to the end zone for a would-be touchdown.

There was no Eagles touchdown because of the forward progress ruling, and the Cowboys scored a touchdown of their own after that to take a 28-10 lead at halftime.

In the first half Williams has three touchdowns, CeeDee Lamb has 57 receiving yards and George Pickens has 49 yards.

Eagles quarterback Joe Milton is playing well, with 145 passing yards and a touchdown, but the Eagles have lost tight end Dallas Goedert and running back Saquon Barkley, and they are going to need something spectacular to mount a second-half comeback against a Cowboys offense that can’t be stopped today.

sports.title: Cowboys' offense rolling over Eagles' defense in Dallas
sports.summary: The Eagles have had no answer for the Cowboys' Javonte Williams, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
sports.body:
Dallas has a 21-3 lead late in the second quarter, and Philadelphia has had no answer for running back Javonte Williams and wide receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.

It hasn’t helped that after Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean was ruled out with a concussion, Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (stinger) and tight end Dallas Goedert (shoulder) both exited the game and were listed as questionable to return. Goedert was later ruled out.

Eagles quarterback Joe Milton is doing his best to move the ball without some of his top weapons, but the injury-plagued Eagles are struggling.

sports.title: Cooper DeJean exits with concussion and Cowboys take lead over Eagles
sports.summary: The Cowboys have taken an early lead in Dallas and the Eagles have lost a top defensive player.
sports.body:
Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean took a hit to the head while making a tackle on the fourth play of the game, went to the locker room for a concussion check, and was quickly ruled out.

The Cowboys’ offense marched down the field on an 11-play, 77-yard drive that ended with a Javonte Williams one-yard touchdown run, and the Cowboys took an early 700 lead.

Eagles quarterback Joe Milton is back in Dallas to face his old team, and if the first drive is any indication, Philadelphia is going to need to Milton and the offense to score plenty of points.

sports.summary: The Buffalo Bills have elevated rookie cornerback Kani Walker from the practice squad ahead of tonight’s game against the Kansas City Chiefs. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills have elevated rookie cornerback Kani Walker from the practice squad ahead of tonight’s game against the Kansas City Chiefs. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2126065974365569364?a=JrwJuRdchVrsq3LlZlg&s=20] Walker, 23, was also elevated for Buffalo’s lone loss of the season, a 29-26 defeat at the hands of the New England Patriots back in Week Four. Walker did not see a snap on defense during that game, but he did make one tackle on 11 special teams snaps. During the preseason, Walker was outstanding for the Bills. He consistently impressed during training camp practices before playing lights-out during the exhibition slate. Walker had 3 tackles, 2 pass breakups, and 1 interception in Buffalo’s three preseason games. Ultimately, he did not make the 53-man roster, but he has remained with the team’s practice squad throughout this season. He has one elevation remaining before the Bills would have to sign him to their 53-man roster in order to have him appear on game day. With Walker’s elevation, that might give a hint as to the availability of top corner Christian Benford, who missed Sunday’s game with a groin injury. Veteran Tre’Davious White came up from the practice squad to replace Benford in that contest. Joining White last Sunday was linebacker Shaq Thompson, who replaced Dorian Williams at linebacker. Given that Walker is the only elevation, it’s safe to assume that Williams will be ready to roll tonight. Does Walker’s elevation mean that Benford is definitely out? We’ll find out when inactives become official 90 minutes before kickoff, which should be right around 6:50 p.m. EDT. Hopefully, our collective turkey-induced food comas will be wearing off by then, and you’ll be able to check back with us before the game begins at 8:20 p.m. EDT.

sports.title: Bears stun Lions on late Rome Odunze TD
sports.summary: The Bears came through at the end of a wild second half in Detroit.
sports.body:
Caleb Williams hit wide receiver Rome Odunze in the back corner of the end zone for a six-yard touchdown with three seconds left on the clock. The extra point gave the Bears a 39-35 lead and the game came to an end after the Lions’ attempt to lateral down the field failed to produce a miracle.

It was the first time the Bears led all day, but that’s all it took for them to end the day in sole possession of first place in the NFC North. Odunze’s score capped a wild second half that saw the two teams put up 55 combined points in one of the most entertaining games of the season.

The game-winning touchdown drive came after Lions head coach Dan Campbell passed on a 51-yard field goal with 2:22 to play in the game and went for it on fourth-and-4. A pass to running back Jahmyr Gibbs was complete, but he was yanked down by linebacker T.J. Edwards and stopped short of a first down.

Campbell’s decisions on the previous possession will also merit a second look. The Lions chose to have Jared Goff roll left to throw on a third-and-1 while in field goal territory and Goff’s pass behind Jameson Williams wound up being intercepted by Bears safety Dillon Thieneman. The Lions chose to run with Sione Vaki rather than Gibbs on the previous play, which was a curious choice on a day when Gibbs ran 21 times for 205 yards and three touchdowns.

That aggressiveness has been a hallmark of the Campbell era, but the calls backfired on a day when the Lions led by as many as 11 points. The defense coming up with big plays to thwart Campbell’s gambles deserves credit for the ultimate result and so does Williams, who finished the day 30-of-44 for 345 yards and two scores despite losing tight end Colston Loveland to a knee injury early in the first quarter.

Williams proved his mettle in big spots several times last season and Thursday’s win is the latest reminder why the Bears are building their future around him. They’ll return home next week for a date with another division leader in the Jaguars and these two teams will do it again in Chicago in Week 17.

The Lions will try to rebound in Atlanta next Sunday and they can’t afford too many more stumbles in a jam-packed NFC playoff race.

sports.title: Aaron Rodgers clears waivers
sports.summary: Rodgers becomes a free agent.
sports.body:
For the third time since March 2025, Rodgers can sign with any team at any time.

The soon-to-be 43-year-old cleared waivers on Thursday, per multiple reports.

He can sign whenever he chooses, either to a practice squad or a 53-man roster. He can wait until the postseason, if he chooses.

Of course, someone will have to want to sign him. In the 2026 offseason, only the Steelers did. At this point, an injury to a starter on a contending team will be the one thing that could create immediate interest in his services.

As long as that team is willing to risk Rodgers eventually dialing up McAfee for another elongated monologue of grievances. At this point, any other outcome would be a surprise.

sports.title: Jahmyr Gibbs up to three touchdowns, Lions up 35-24
sports.summary: Gibbs broke free for 70 yards this time.
sports.body:
Gibbs broke free for a 70-yard touchdown with 8:20 left to play in the game and the Lions now have a 35-24 lead over the Bears. It is Gibbs’s second three-touchdown game of the season and he is up to 18 total touchdowns for the season.

The Bears could have gone to a 12-point lead, but Cairo Santos missed an extended extra point after Christian Mahogany was flagged for taunting on the touchdown run.

Gibbs’s score came after the Lions forced the first punt of the second half by either team and the Bears will now have to scramble in order to find a way to end the day on top of the NFC North.

If they can’t, their inability to contain Gibbs will be a big reason for the loss. He has 20 carries for 171 yards and four catches for 41 yards as the Lions try for their seventh straight win.

sports.title: Carson Beck remains out of Cardinals practice
sports.summary: It looks like the Cardinals are on track to be without Carson Beck against the Commanders this week.
sports.body:
The quarterback missed practice for the second straight day due to the back injury that kept him from playing in last Sunday’s loss to the Chiefs. Beck made his first NFL start in Week 10, but the lack of practice work points to veteran Josh Johnson making another start for a team he joined in the last month.

Guard Jon Gaines (ankle) and linebacker Josh Sweat (rest, shoulder) were also out of practice on Thursday.

Tight end Hunter Long (ankle), linebacker Karson Sharar (groin), and linebacker Cody Simon (calf) were limited participants. Safety Budda Baker (rest, elbow), center Hjalte Froholdt (rest), guard Isaac Seumalo (rest), linebacker Mack Wilson (rest), and defensive lineman Zach Carter (knee) were all full participants.

sports.title: Matt LaFleur on Packers' run-game struggles: "We're trying"
sports.summary: The Packers weren't able to stop the run on Wednesday against the Rams.
sports.body:
“Right now, we’re a pass-heavy offense and we’re trying to sneak in some runs there to at least keep the defense honest,” coach Matt LaFleur told reporters after the 26-13 loss when asked about his team’s offensive identity.

“Obviously not, not when you lose the game like that,” LaFleur said. “So I would say the answer to your question is no. I mean, you’ve got to convert third downs too. You’ve got to get those opportunities to get some first downs. And the second half, I think we had one drive that was a seven-play drive or whatever and everything else was like three-and-out or two-and-out and we turned the ball over.”

On a night when the Rams had 241 yards rushing against only 132 yards passing, the Packers mustered only 55 rushing yards on 14 attempts.

Not having Josh Jacobs didn’t help matters. Without Jacobs (who’s recovering from a broken finger), the Packers’ backfield consisted of Kaleb Johnson (eight carries for 13 yards), MarShawn Lloyd (one carry for 10 yards), and Chris Brooks (one carry for four yards).

Receiver Savion Williams ran the ball twice for 18 yards, making him the leading rusher for Green Bay. Quarterback Jordan Love added one for seven, and receiver Bo Melton ran one time, for three yards.

And, no, that’s not good enough. Especially on a night when receiver Christian Watson was lost early to a concussion.

Even if the Packers can muster enough wins over the final six weeks to qualify for the postseason, it will become very hard to win in January if they can’t run or stop the run.

sports.title: Bears back within 26-24 on D'Andre Swift TD run
sports.summary: The Bears and Lions are lighting up the scoreboard in the second half.
sports.body:
Bears running back D’Andre Swift broke loose for a 30-yard touchdown with 3:09 left in the third quarter. The score made it 26-24 Lions and was the third touchdown in three total possessions for the NFC North teams since halftime.

Swift also had an 18-yard catch during the drive and he has 134 yards from scrimmage already this afternoon. Kyle Monangai ran for the first two Bears touchdowns and the team now has 126 yards on the ground on Thanksgiving.

The Bears have shown they can put points on the board. Now they need to show they can make enough stops to make them winners.

sports.title: Jahmyr Gibbs scores again, Lions lead 26-17
sports.summary: Gibbs is up to 17 touchdowns on the season.
sports.body:
Gibbs scored his second touchdown of the game with 5:45 to play in the third quarter and the Lions moved their lead over the Bears to 26-17. It’s the third straight game with multiple touchdowns for the Lions star.

Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown is another star for Detroit and he made a tough catch to pick up 17 yards on the way to the end zone. He also drew a pass interference penalty to set the Lions up on the 1-yard-line and Gibbs took care of things from there.

The Bears rallied for a touchdown to open the second half, but they’re going to need to start getting some defensive stops to pull off a comeback win in Detroit.

sports.title: Bears cut Lions lead to 19-17 on Kyle Monangai's second TD
sports.summary: The Bears opened the second half with a touchdown drive.
sports.body:
Running back Kyle Monangai scored his second touchdown of the game to cap the team’s first possession of the third quarter and the Lions’ lead has been slashed to 19-17.

Monangai also had a 14-yard pass reception on the drive and Caleb Williams picked up 25 more with a strike to wide receiver Luther Burden. The running back now has five touchdowns this season and it is his second multi-score game of the year.

The Lions will try to put more breathing room between themselves and the Bears when they get the ball for the first time since the halftime break.

sports.title: Lions score nine quick points before halftime, lead Bears 19-10
sports.summary: A safety and a touchdown have the home team up after 30 minutes of play.
sports.body:
Defensive end Derrick Moore forced Bears quarterback Caleb Williams to fumble on a sack in the end zone and Bears tackle Darnell Wright was flagged for batting the ball back into the field of play. That’s a safety and Lions head coach Dan Campbell opted to accept that rather than decline the penalty and take the ball on the Chicago 14-yard-line.

That choice paid off with more points for the Lions. Jared Goff and Jameson Williams hooked up for a 39-yard gain to move the ball deep into Bears territory and Goff found tight end Sam LaPorta for an 11-yard touchdown with six seconds to play in the half. That pushed Detroit’s lead to 19-10 at halftime.

The Bears will get the ball coming out of the locker room, but the two scores make for a big swing in momentum after the Bears erased a 10-point deficit earlier in the second quarter.

Goff is 13-of-22 for 193 yards and Jahmyr Gibbs has 98 yards from scrimmage. Gibbs also scored his 16th touchdown of the season earlier in the game.

The Bears lost tight end Colston Loveland to a knee injury early in the game, so he won’t be part of any comeback effort that Chicago is able to put together in the final 30 minutes.

sports.title: Steelers activate Michael Pittman Jr., sign Max Hurleman to active roster
sports.summary: Mason Rudolph will have wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. available as a target in his first start of the 2026 season.
sports.body:
The Steelers activated Pittman from injured reserve on Thursday, which sets him up to face the Broncos on Friday afternoon. Pittman had seven catches for 89 yards in the first three games of the season.

Rudolph will also be able to throw to Max Hurleman. Hurleman was a topic of conversation at Aaron Rodgers’s final press conference as a member of the Steelers because Rodgers questioned why the front office did not have him on the active roster.

The team remedied that on Thursday, but Rodgers will not be able to benefit since he was released after far more critical comments about the organization in the wake of his benching on Tuesday night.

Wide receiver Ben Skowronek was placed on injured reserve and the Steelers also elevated offensive lineman Doug Nester and linebacker Jacoby Windmon from the practice squad.

sports.title: Bears tie Lions 10-10 on Kyle Monangai TD
sports.summary: The Bears spotted the Lions a 10-point lead in the second quarter, but they've wiped it out with four minutes to go in the first half.
sports.body:
Running back Kyle Monangai scored from a yard out to make it 10-10 in Detroit. The touchdown capped an eight-play, 80-yard drive that saw Monangai’s backfield mate D’Andre Swift account for the longest gain.

Swift caught a short pass from Caleb Williams and followed downfield blocks for a 33-yard gain. Williams also completed a pair of passes to tight end Stephen Carlson for 30 yards on the way to the end zone.

Those were Carlson’s first two catches of the season and the Bears may continue to look his way now that they’ve lost Colston Loveland to a knee injury.

sports.body: To say that Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau is having a career year in 2026 is quite the understatement. Rousseau leads the NFL in quarterback hits with 29, and is currently second league-wide with 10 sacks in 10 games this season. His current sack total is a new career high for Rousseau — the first time in his professional career he’s reach double-digits in that category. Rousseau deserves to be mentioned in NFL Defensive Player of the Year conversations. He seems to be a good candidate as an All-Pro selection, and is likely to receive Pro Bowl honors. His success comes following a switch this offseason to 3-4 outside linebacker after playing the previous five seasons as a defensive end in a 4-3 system. It’s the first time in Rousseau’s career that he’s played that role as an edge rusher out wide from the linebacker box. When you run through Rousseau’s stats this year, it’s easy to imagine that he’s thrilled with the position shift. In just over half a season to this point, Rousseau has set new career highs in sacks (10), quarterback hits (29), and pass defenses (8); while tying his career high in forced fumbles (3), and remains just four off his single-season-career-best of 16 tackles for loss. When new Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady hired Jim Leonhard as the team’s current defensive coordinator, many were very curious how the former Bills safety intended to implement the attack-based system he espoused. After all, Leonhard had never called a team’s defensive plays at the NFL level, and he decided to make sweeping changes while marching forward with a large group of players hand-picked by prior head coach Sean McDermott. With the benefit of hindsight, it’s now clear that Rousseau may have been miscast as a do-it-all defensive end left to battle it out in the trenches. He played well there for McDermott, of course, but the brand of game-wrecking energy now regularly seen was at best available in spurts with him so deeply tied up in close hand combat against offensive linemen.
